instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Gen 38:15 'thought' is reckoning or taking someone for something: Judah takes the veiled woman for a prostitute. Verses: Gen 38:15.
observations.grounds: he thought she was a prostitute

observations.text: In Psa 73:16 'thought' is to reflect and try to understand: the psalmist turns the matter over and finds it wearisome until he enters the sanctuary. Verses: Psa 73:16.
observations.grounds: when I thought how to understand this

observations.text: In Ecc 9:10 'thought' is the Hebrew noun for reckoning or account: the verse says there is no work, reckoning, knowledge or wisdom in Sheol. Verses: Ecc 9:10.
observations.grounds: no work or thought or knowledge

observations.text: In 1Ch 28:9 'thought' is the Hebrew word for a plan or device that the Lord understands, with every heart searched; David tells Solomon to serve with a whole heart. Verses: 1Ch 28:9.
In 2Sa 3:19 'thought good' renders the Hebrew word for eye in the idiom 'in the eyes of': what seemed good to Israel and Benjamin. Verses: 2Sa 3:19.
In Jon 1:6 'give a thought' is the Hebrew verb of taking thought or caring: the captain hopes the god will think of them so they may not perish. Verses: Jon 1:6.
observations.grounds: will give a thought to us

observations.text: In Job 12:5 'thought' is the Hebrew noun for the settled thinking of the one at ease: it despises misfortune. The verse ties the thought to the circumstance of ease. Verses: Job 12:5.
observations.grounds: thought of one who is at ease

observations.text: In Mic 2:8 'with no thought of war' is the Hebrew verb of turning back from war: the trusting passers-by who are stripped have returned from fighting. Verses: Mic 2:8.
In Amo 4:13 'thought' is the Hebrew word for musing or meditation: God declares to man what his own thought is, as the maker of mountains and wind. Verses: Amo 4:13.
observations.grounds: declares to man what is his thought

observations.text: God's thoughts, and the contrast with man's: his thoughts toward his people are many and very deep, the nations do not know the Lord's thoughts, his thoughts are not man's and are as high above them as the heavens, and his thoughts are precious to the psalmist. The thoughts are the Lord's own purposes and mind. Verses: Psa 40:5, Psa 92:5, Psa 139:17, Isa 55:8, Isa 55:9, Mic 4:12.

Conceiving evil as if in a womb: wicked people conceive trouble, chaff and mischief and give birth to evil, stubble and iniquity. The same verb of conceiving is turned to what a person forms within and brings out in act. Verses: Job 15:35, Isa 33:11, Isa 59:4.

Conceiving a child: the woman becomes pregnant and bears, in the promises and announcements of a son, in the question of the barren, in the cleansed woman who will conceive, in the confession of the psalmist that his mother conceived him in sin, and in the sign of the virgin. The words are Hebrew and Greek verbs and nouns of pregnancy and seed, and the English 'conceive' is bodily. Verses: Num 5:28, Num 11:12, Judg 13:3, Judg 13:5, Judg 13:7, Psa 51:5, Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23, Luk 1:31, Heb 11:11.

'Opinion' in the phrase about not caring for anyone's opinion: the Greek verb is of looking, and the phrase is that Jesus does not look at the person's face, that is, does not weigh people by standing. It is regard for status, not a view held. Verses: Mat 22:16, Mar 12:14.

Opinion as a view that a person holds and declares: Elihu is afraid to declare his opinion and then insists on it, and the fool takes pleasure only in declaring what his heart holds. It is a person's own view, set against understanding. Verses: Job 32:6, Job 32:10, Job 32:17, Pro 18:2.
'Perhaps' as the captain's hope that the god may give a thought to them: the Hebrew particle of possibility, carrying no thinking of its own. Verses: Jon 1:6.
'With no thought of war' as turning back from war: the Hebrew verb is of returning, said of the trusting passers-by who are stripped. It is a turning back, not a thought. Verses: Mic 2:8.
'Well thought of' as a good report: the Greek noun is of testimony, the overseer must have a good report from outsiders. It is how others speak of him, not what he thinks. Verses: 1Ti 3:7.

Thinking as the way the mind works, its understanding or frame: the thinking of people who knew God becomes futile, the believers are to be mature and not children in their thinking, and they are to arm themselves with Christ's way of thinking. It is the mind's mode, with a measure of maturity or futility. Verses: Rom 1:21, 1Cor 14:20, 1Pe 4:1.

A question that asks for a hearer's view: 'what do you think?' is put to Simon, to the hearers, to the lawyer, to the chief priests and to those looking for Jesus. It asks the person to give a judgment he already forms. Verses: Mat 17:25, Mat 18:12, Mat 21:28, Mat 22:17, Mat 22:42, Luk 10:36, Joh 11:56.

What seems right or best in someone's eyes: the Hebrew word for eye in the idiom of what appears good to a person, rendered think, think best or thought good. It is a person's own judgment of what is good or fitting. Verses: Num 36:6, 2Sa 10:3, 1Ch 19:3, Jer 40:4, Jer 40:5, 2Sa 3:19.

A thought quoted as inner speech: the Hebrew verb of saying introduces what a person says in himself, and the quoted sentence gives the thought; the Greek of Luk 12:17 does the same with the rich man's words to himself. The thought is inner speech, usually about what others will do or what will follow, and the verse often shows it wrong. Verses: Gen 32:8, 1Sa 27:11, 1Sa 27:12, 2Sa 5:6, 2Ki 7:12, 2Ch 32:1, Neh 6:9, Psa 64:5, 1Sa 20:3, Gen 20:11, Gen 26:9, Gen 31:31, Gen 32:20, Exo 2:14, Jos 22:28, Judg 3:24, Judg 15:2, Rut 4:4, 1Sa 16:6, 1Sa 18:11, 1Sa 18:17, 1Sa 18:21, 1Sa 20:26, 2Sa 14:15, 2Sa 14:17, 2Sa 21:16, 2Ki 5:11, 2Ki 20:19, Job 29:18, Psa 94:18, Isa 39:8, Jer 3:7, Jer 3:19, Eze 20:32, Luk 12:17.

Planning or intending: the Assyrian's heart is set on destroying nations, the prophets intend to make the people forget the name, the Lord plans for his people what they planned, and the one who speaks against God intends to change times and laws. The verbs are of devising and purpose. Verses: Job 6:26, Isa 10:7, Jer 23:27, Dan 7:25, Num 33:56, 1Sa 18:25.

Giving thought to something: calling to mind, reflecting on, attending to, taking thought for or turning the mind to what is named: the psalmist thinks on his ways and on the Lord's rules, the Lord takes thought for the poor, the prudent give thought to their steps, the believer is to think on what is excellent, Jerusalem took no thought of her end. The word is attention of the mind to a matter or person. Verses: Psa 119:52, Psa 119:59, Psa 144:3, Mat 9:4, Eph 3:20, Phili 4:8, Heb 11:15, Psa 40:17, Psa 48:9, Psa 73:16, Pro 14:15, Pro 21:29, Lam 1:9, Jon 1:6.

Reckoning something as so, judging or counting: Paul judges it necessary, a thing is counted unclean by the one who holds it so, the unbelief of Act 26:8 is judged incredible, Judah takes the covered woman for a prostitute, and Job 41:32 counts the deep as white-haired. The word is a judgment that counts or takes something as of a certain kind. Verses: Job 35:2, Job 41:32, 2Cor 12:6, 2Pe 1:13, Rom 14:14, Gen 38:15, Act 26:8, 2Cor 9:5, Phili 2:25.

Being minded: the way a person is set in mind, to rate oneself soberly in Rom 12:3, to hold the same mind or another in Phili 3:15, and the child's mindedness given up in 1Cor 13:11. The Greek verb is of being of a mind or having an attitude. Verses: Rom 12:3, Phili 3:15, 1Cor 13:11.
observations.grounds: to think, regard, hold an opinion

observations.text: Thoughts as purposes and devices: the intention of the heart in Gen 6:5, the schemes of the wicked, the thoughts the righteous and the wicked hold, the thoughts to be forsaken, and the wicked thoughts that lodge within. The word is of purpose, plan and device, and the verses place it in the heart. Verses: 1Ch 28:9, Gen 6:5, 1Ch 29:18, Job 21:27, Psa 10:4, Psa 56:5, Psa 94:11, Pro 12:5, Pro 15:26, Isa 55:7, Isa 59:7, Isa 66:18, Jer 4:14, Lam 3:62.

Thoughts as what arises and is held in the mind, known to God or others: they come out of the heart, are perceived by Jesus, are alarmed or answered, are known by the spirit of the person or by the Lord, are shaped by ease, and are led astray. The words are nouns of thought, reasoning and musing, in many Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek words, with the heart or the mind as their place. Verses: Deu 15:9, Job 12:5, Ecc 9:10, Amo 4:13, 2Cor 10:5, Job 20:2, Psa 139:2, Psa 139:23, Ecc 10:20, Eze 38:10, Dan 2:29, Dan 2:30, Dan 4:19, Dan 5:6, Dan 5:10, Dan 7:28, Mat 12:25, Mat 15:19, Mar 7:21, Luk 1:51, Luk 2:35, Luk 5:22, Luk 6:8, Luk 11:17, 1Cor 2:11, 1Cor 3:20, 2Cor 11:3, Heb 4:12, Jam 2:4.

Supposing, holding a belief or imagining something to be so: the belief is stated or put in question, often about oneself or about another, and the verse tests, corrects or reproves it. The hearers think the Gentiles' many words will be heard, that Jesus cannot appeal to his Father, that he came to give peace, that they are wise, stand, or are religious; in the Hebrew verses the speaker is told what the hearer thinks or the Lord says what the house of Israel thinks. The word is a belief held and not yet tested. Verses: 2Sa 18:27, 2Ki 18:20, 2Ch 13:8, Est 4:13, Isa 36:5, Eze 11:5, Mat 5:17, Mat 6:7, Mat 10:34, Mat 26:53, Luk 12:51, Luk 13:2, Luk 13:4, Joh 5:39, Joh 5:45, Joh 16:2, Act 17:29, 1Cor 4:9, 1Cor 7:26, 1Cor 7:40, 1Cor 12:23, 2Cor 11:16, Heb 10:29, 2Cor 12:19, Phili 1:17, Luk 8:18, 1Cor 3:18, 1Cor 7:36, 1Cor 10:12, 1Cor 14:37, Gal 6:3, Phili 3:4, Jam 1:26, Psa 50:21, Mat 20:10, Mar 6:49, Luk 24:37, Joh 11:13, Joh 13:29, Act 8:20, Act 12:9.

The codes of God's thoughts are H4284 (thought, device; plan, purpose) and H7454 (purpose, aim, thought). The lexicon bears out thoughts as purposes, here the Lord's own, set against man's in Isa 55:8 and Isa 55:9 and unknown to the nations in Mic 4:12.

The code of conceiving evil is H2029 (to conceive, become pregnant, bear). The lexicon gives only the bodily sense; Job 15:35, Isa 33:11 and Isa 59:4 turn it to trouble and mischief formed within and brought out: the figure is the verses', not the lexicon's.

The codes of conceiving a child are H2029 (to conceive), H2030A (pregnant), H2232 (to sow; to be made pregnant), H3179 (to be hot, conceive), G4815 (to become pregnant, conceive), G2602 (foundation, with the seed in Heb 11:11) and G4690G (seed, offspring); G1722 (in) and G2192 (to have) make the Greek phrase of having in the womb. The lexicon bears out a bodily conceiving with no act of thought.

The code behind opinion in Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 is G0991 (to see, look at). The lexicon gives seeing; the phrase is not looking at a person's standing, so no view is held: the English opinion is not the code's sense.

The codes of a declared opinion are H1843 (knowledge, opinion; judgment) in Job 32:6, Job 32:10 and Job 32:17 and H3820A (inner man, mind, heart) in Pro 18:2, where the fool's opinion is what is in his heart. The lexicon bears out a view held and spoken.
The code of thought in Jon 1:6 is H0194 (perhaps, peradventure). The lexicon gives a particle of possibility; it carries no thinking, and the giving of thought is the captain's hope about the god.
The code of with no thought of war in Mic 2:8 is H7725G (to return, turn back). The lexicon gives returning; the English thought is not in the code.
The code of well thought of in 1Ti 3:7 is G3141 (testimony; good reputation). The lexicon bears out a good report from others, not a thought of the overseer.

The codes of thinking as the mind's mode are G1261 (reasoning, thought) in Rom 1:21, G5424 (thinking, understanding) in 1Cor 14:20 and G1771 (attitude, thought, intention) in 1Pe 4:1. G2532 (and) is a connective in the unit. The lexicon bears out the mind's way of working, with futility or maturity named by the verses.

The code of what do you think is G1380 (to think, consider, regard; an action of the mind and heart for processing information into understanding and choices). The lexicon bears out asking for a judgment the hearer forms, in Mat 17:25, Mat 18:12, Mat 21:28, Mat 22:17, Mat 22:42, Luk 10:36 and Joh 11:56.
observations.grounds: an action of the mind and heart

observations.text: The code of what seems best is H5869I (eye; as showing mental qualities), with H0413 (to, toward). The lexicon bears out the eye as the seat of judgment in the idiom good in your eyes, in Num 36:6, 2Sa 10:3, 1Ch 19:3, Jer 40:4, Jer 40:5 and 2Sa 3:19.

The codes of a thought quoted as inner speech are H0559 (to say; to say in one's heart, to think, to intend), G1260 (to reason, deliberate) and G3004G (to say). H0834A (which), H0853 (the object marker) and H3588A (that, for) are small words in the units. The lexicon bears out saying in one's heart as the form of the thought, as in 1Sa 16:6, 1Sa 18:11, 1Sa 18:17 and 1Sa 20:3.
observations.grounds: to say in one's heart, to think
